title: Improved genotyping of the dysferlin null mouse
protocol: Add 0.5 ml Lysis buffer to a 1.5 ml tube containing mouse ear or tail clip and incubate for a minimum of 3 hours to overnight at 55 ºC while shaking at 200 rpm.
After lysis, vortex the tube to disrupt the tissue.
Spin the mixture at 20,000 g for 10 minutes with hinges oriented to the outside.
Pipette 500 µl of isopropanol into a new tube.
Decant the lysis supernatant into the isopropanol-containing tube after centrifugation.
Invert the tube several times to mix and incubate at room temperature for at least 5 minutes.
Spin the mixture at 20,000 g for 10 minutes to pellet the DNA.
Pour off the supernatant.
Wash the pellet by adding 0.5 ml of 70% ethanol and vortex briefly.
Spin the tube at 20,000 g for 5 minutes.
Pour off the 70% ethanol, invert the tubes and air-dry for 5 minutes.
Remove residual ethanol with an aspirator.
Resuspend the DNA in 500 µl of 10 mM Tris, pH 8.0.
Shake at 200 rpm at 55 ºC for 20 minutes to overnight to facilitate DNA resuspension.
Vortex all reagents after thawing and spin briefly.
Keep all reagents on ice until use.
Prepare the reaction mixture on ice.
Preset a thermal cycler ready to start the designated program.
Prepare a Master Mix of PCR reagents for all samples plus two additional reactions, excluding mouse DNA template.
Mix the components of the Master Mix in the order listed, except for LA Taq enzyme (add last).
Gently flick the Master Mix tube to mix and spin briefly.
Dispense 9.5 μl of Master Mix into each PCR tube for every sample.
Add 0.5 μl of DNA samples and controls to corresponding PCR tubes.
Spin PCR tubes to mix the DNA and PCR Master Mix.
Place PCR tubes in thermal cycler and run the program shown below.
Prepare a 0.8% agarose gel using TAE buffer.
Add 2 μl Orange G Loading dye to each reaction.
Electrophorese 4 μl of amplified product per 5mm wide gel lane with 0.4 ug/ml EtBr in running buffer.
Run the gel slowly at 100 volts for 30 to 45 minutes to resolve the 4846 bp and 3904 bp bands.
Document the gel image to interpret genotype.
Determine the length of the amplified product using the marker standard.
